opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alexandra Johnson (employee ID E003) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E003.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Alexandra Johnson (E003) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin on Source Code. Full-time employees max is write unless their role owns the system; Analyst does not own Source Code, so admin is not permitted. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security check: Alexandra Johnson (E003) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read (write only with advanced training, never admin). Since admin is requested but not permitted, recommend granting read.
reason: Requested admin on Source Code. HR reports E003 as full-time Analyst (max write, since Analyst does not own Source Code), while Security reports E003 as a contractor with basic security training (max read, never admin). The facts conflict, so I apply the more restrictive valid interpretation: contractor with basic training → max is read. Admin is not permitted under either interpretation, and read does not exceed any policy limit, so I grant read.
